title: Circles
subtitle: Radius, Circumference, Area & π
bounds: PROTOCOL §4b measurement. Every given radius or diameter is 2-10 (a halved diameter is even, so its radius is 2-5; tier 1 alone halves an odd diameter to x.5). Every × step has both factors 1-10; every ÷ is exact with divisor and quotient 2-10; every + joins two values of 20 or less. Answers stay in terms of π: every π coefficient (circumference, area, arc, perimeter) is a whole number 1-100. 'Use 3 for π' answers are whole numbers 1-100 reached through times-table steps (6 × r, 3 × d, 3 × 3 × 3). Half- and quarter-circle areas go through an even radius ((r/2) × r, (r/2) × (r/2)). Scale questions use factors 1/2, 2, 3, 4. No area-to-radius (square roots are grade 8). Wrong choices up to 999.

tiers.name: Radius, Diameter & π
tiers.description: Radius is half the diameter. Circumference ÷ diameter is π for every circle.

tiers.name: Circumference
tiers.description: Distance around: C = 2πr = πd. Leave π as π.

tiers.name: Area of a Circle
tiers.description: Area = π × r × r. Square the radius, not the diameter.

tiers.name: Work Backward & Estimate
tiers.description: Find the radius from the circumference. Use 3 for π to estimate.

tiers.name: Half & Quarter Circles
tiers.description: Areas, curved edges and perimeters of parts of a circle.

HALVED_FOR_DOUBLED.student: Diameter is twice the radius: it goes all the way across.
HALVED_FOR_DOUBLED.teacher: Halves the radius to get the diameter.

DOUBLED_FOR_HALVED.student: Radius is half the diameter: it only goes to the center.
DOUBLED_FOR_HALVED.teacher: Doubles the diameter to get the radius.

SAME_NUMBER.student: Radius and diameter are different: the diameter is twice the radius.
SAME_NUMBER.teacher: Gives the same number for radius and diameter.

C_FOR_D.student: Diameter is straight across. The distance around needs π.
C_FOR_D.teacher: Reports the circumference where the diameter is asked.

HALVED_TWICE.student: Halve just once: the radius is half the diameter.
HALVED_TWICE.teacher: Halves twice (divides by 4) going from diameter to radius.

SIZE_MATTERS.student: The ratio does not depend on size. Every circle gives the same number.
SIZE_MATTERS.teacher: Answers with the given length instead of the constant ratio.

TWO_PI.student: π is circumference ÷ diameter. The 2π is circumference ÷ radius.
TWO_PI.teacher: Gives 2π for circumference ÷ diameter (mixes in the 2 of C = 2πr).

DIAMETER_RATIO.student: Circumference ÷ radius is 2π. Only ÷ diameter gives π.
DIAMETER_RATIO.teacher: Gives π for circumference ÷ radius (uses the diameter ratio).

INVERTED.student: You flipped it: the circumference is the big number on top.
INVERTED.teacher: Divides the other way round (diameter or radius ÷ circumference).

VOCAB_MIX.student: Around = circumference, inside = area, across = diameter, center-out = radius.

RADII_COUNT.student: Those are radii. A diameter is 2 radii, so about 3 diameters.
RADII_COUNT.teacher: Counts radii when the question asks for diameters.

DIAMETER_COUNT.student: Those are diameters. A diameter is 2 radii: about 6 radii.
DIAMETER_COUNT.teacher: Counts diameters when the question asks for radii.

SQUARE_AROUND.student: A square around it is longer. A circle is about 3 diameters, 6 radii.
SQUARE_AROUND.teacher: Uses the perimeter of the bounding square (4 diameters or 8 radii).

R_FOR_D.student: Circumference = π × diameter. The radius is only half of that.
R_FOR_D.teacher: Uses πr (the radius) where π × diameter is needed.

AREA_FOR_C.student: That's the area. Circumference goes around the edge: 2πr, or π × diameter.
AREA_FOR_C.teacher: Computes the area (or squares a length) instead of the circumference.

DOUBLED_D.student: Too much: circumference is π × diameter, or 2 × π × radius. Not both 2s.
DOUBLED_D.teacher: Doubles the diameter: applies 2πr with the diameter in place of r.

NO_PI.student: Don't drop π: it is part of every circle formula (use 3 if told).
NO_PI.teacher: Leaves π out of the answer.

D_FOR_R.student: In π × r × r, r is the RADIUS. Use half the diameter.
D_FOR_R.teacher: Uses the diameter where the radius belongs (squares the diameter).

DOUBLED_RADIUS.student: Square the radius as given: π × r × r. Don't double it first.
DOUBLED_RADIUS.teacher: Doubles the radius (uses the diameter) before squaring.

SQUARED_SCALE.student: Circumference is a length: double the radius, double the circumference.
SQUARED_SCALE.teacher: Scales the circumference by the square of the radius factor.

C_FOR_AREA.student: That's the circumference. Area is π × radius × radius.
C_FOR_AREA.teacher: Computes the circumference instead of the area.

NO_SQUARE.student: Area needs r × r: square the radius, don't just use it.
NO_SQUARE.teacher: Multiplies by the radius once instead of squaring it.

SAME_SCALE.student: Area uses r × r, so it grows by the scale factor squared.
SAME_SCALE.teacher: Scales the area by the same factor as the radius.

CUBED_SCALE.student: Cubing is for volume. Lengths scale by k, areas by k × k.
CUBED_SCALE.teacher: Scales the circumference or area by the cube of the radius factor.

SUM_RADII.student: Add the AREAS, not the radii. Find each π × r × r first, then add.
SUM_RADII.teacher: Adds the radii first, then finds one area.

ONE_CIRCLE.student: You used only one circle. Add both areas.
ONE_CIRCLE.teacher: Reports the area of only one of the two circles.

GAVE_DIAMETER.student: The number beside π is the diameter. The radius is half of it.
GAVE_DIAMETER.teacher: Reads the π coefficient (the diameter) as the radius.

WRONG_WAY.student: Going backward means undoing: divide here, don't multiply.
WRONG_WAY.teacher: Multiplies instead of dividing when working back from the circumference.

GAVE_RADIUS.student: The number beside π is the diameter itself, not half of it.
GAVE_RADIUS.teacher: Halves the π coefficient to give the radius when the diameter is asked.

FORGOT_PI.student: Don't forget π (3 here): C = 6 × radius, or 3 × diameter.
FORGOT_PI.teacher: Ignores π when working back from an estimated circumference.

WHOLE_CIRCLE.student: That's the whole circle. Take only the half or quarter you need.
WHOLE_CIRCLE.teacher: Reports the whole circle's measure for a part of a circle.

HALVED_RADIUS.student: Half the circle means half the AREA, not half the radius.
HALVED_RADIUS.teacher: Halves the radius before squaring instead of halving the area.

ARC_FOR_AREA.student: That's the curved edge. Area is the space inside.
ARC_FOR_AREA.teacher: Gives the length of the curved edge where the area is asked.

HALF_FOR_QUARTER.student: A quarter is 1/4 of the circle, not 1/2.
HALF_FOR_QUARTER.teacher: Takes half of the circle for a quarter circle.

QUARTERED_RADIUS.student: Take 1/4 of the area, not 1/4 of the radius.
QUARTERED_RADIUS.teacher: Quarters the radius before squaring instead of quartering the area.

AREA_FOR_ARC.student: That's area. The curved edge is a length: part of the circumference.
AREA_FOR_ARC.teacher: Gives the area where the curved edge is asked.

PERIMETER_NOT_ARC.student: That adds the flat side. The curved edge alone is just the curve.
PERIMETER_NOT_ARC.teacher: Adds the diameter (the flat side) to the curved edge.

ARC_ONLY.student: Perimeter also includes the flat side: add the diameter.
ARC_ONLY.teacher: Gives only the curved edge for the perimeter of a semicircle.

WHOLE_C_PLUS.student: Only half the circumference is curved. Then add the diameter.
WHOLE_C_PLUS.teacher: Uses the whole circumference plus the diameter for a semicircle.

HALF_C_PLUS_R.student: The flat side is the whole diameter, not just the radius.
HALF_C_PLUS_R.teacher: Adds the radius, not the diameter, as the flat side.
